decisions.context: The brief describes high daily volume, strong seasonal variation, multiple consumers, and a need to detect quality drift. These drive the architecture in this order.
decisions.rationale: Scale and variable demand shape the processing and cost choices; drift visibility and team access shape monitoring and delivery.

decisions.decision: Process documents through a durable asynchronous queue
decisions.context: Millions of classifications per day and seasonal peaks make synchronous, tightly coupled processing difficult to scale. A queue can buffer bursts and let workers scale with demand.
decisions.rationale: Millions per day and seasonal variation decide in favor of buffering and elastic workers; this adds queue operations and can increase end-to-end latency.
consequences: Workers need retry and idempotency handling.
Queue depth becomes a capacity signal.

decisions.decision: Expose results through a shared results interface
decisions.context: Several teams consume the classifications, so a common result contract avoids making each team depend directly on classifier internals. The brief does not specify whether consumers need push or pull access.

alternatives.label: Shared result store with documented API
cons: Teams: requires API and schema ownership

alternatives.label: Publish results to each team separately

chosen.label: Shared result store with documented API

decisions.rationale: Several consumers decide in favor of one shared contract; teams give up some delivery customization and must coordinate on schema changes.
consequences: Define stable fields for class, confidence, and processing status.
Consumer access patterns and freshness needs remain to be specified.

decisions.decision: Track classification quality by model and prompt version
decisions.context: Operators need to see when quality drifts. Recording the model and prompt version with results makes observed changes traceable to classifier changes.

alternatives.label: Versioned results with drift dashboards and alerts
pros: Drift: relate changes to model versions
cons: Drift: needs quality signals or review labels

chosen.label: Versioned results with drift dashboards and alerts

decisions.rationale: The need to detect quality drift decides in favor of quality monitoring and version attribution; this requires suitable quality signals, which the brief does not define.
consequences: Persist model and prompt versions with each result.
Define drift thresholds and alert ownership.

uncovered: Document privacy, security, and data residency constraints
Classification taxonomy and confidence-based escalation rules
Quality labels or review process for measuring drift
Consumer-specific access patterns and availability targets
